`aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng` lists `aws_iam_role.managed_ng` in `depends_on`, but it already references `aws_iam_role.managed_ng.arn` via `node_role_arn`, so the implicit dependency already orders it after the role. The explicit entry adds nothing (the instance-profile and policy-attachment entries are still needed).

`null_resource.update_trust_policy` depends_on `kubernetes_namespace.spark`, but its local-exec command already interpolates `${kubernetes_namespace.spark.id}`, which creates the same implicit dependency.

`null_resource.update_trust_policy` depends_on `aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution`, but the command already interpolates `${aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id}`, so the dependency is already implicit.

`aws_eks_addon.vpc_cni` sets `service_account_role_arn = module.irsa_addon.irsa_iam_role_arn`, which already creates an implicit dependency on `module.irsa_addon`. Listing `module.irsa_addon` again in `depends_on` is redundant.

`aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver` reads `module.irsa_addon.irsa_iam_role_arn` for `service_account_role_arn`, so `module.irsa_addon` is already an implicit dependency; the explicit `depends_on = [module.irsa_addon]` duplicates it.

`module.aws_eks_teams` passes `eks_cluster_id = module.aws_eks.cluster_id` and `tags = module.eks_tags.tags`, so it already depends implicitly on `module.aws_eks`; the explicit `depends_on = [module.aws_eks]` is entirely redundant.

`module.aws_eks_fargate_profiles` passes `eks_cluster_id = module.aws_eks.cluster_id`, so `module.aws_eks` is already an implicit dependency. Only the `kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth` element of the `depends_on` list is actually needed.

`module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups` already depends implicitly on `module.aws_eks` through `eks_cluster_id`, `cluster_ca_base64`, `cluster_endpoint` and the security-group ids; the `module.aws_eks` entry in `depends_on` is redundant (the `kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth` entry is still required).

`module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups` references many `module.aws_eks` outputs (cluster id, endpoint, CA, security groups), so the implicit dependency already exists; the `module.aws_eks` element of `depends_on` duplicates it.

`module.emr_on_eks` passes `eks_cluster_id = module.aws_eks.cluster_id`, so `module.aws_eks` is already an implicit dependency; only the `kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth` entry in `depends_on` adds new ordering.

`kubernetes_deployment.aws_otel_eks_sidecar` places its pods in namespace `aws-otel-eks` using a hard-coded local string instead of a reference to `kubernetes_namespace.aws_otel_eks`, so Terraform may attempt to create the deployment before the namespace exists and the apply fails with "namespaces \"aws-otel-eks\" not found".

`kubernetes_role_binding.emr_containers` refers to its role by the literal `local.emr_service_name` string rather than to `kubernetes_role.emr_containers`, so nothing forces the Role to be created first and the binding can fail at apply time with "roles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io \"emr-containers\" not found".
